# TCP Fast Open

## Thesis

**TCP Fast Open (TFO)** lets a client send data in the first SYN (with a cookie) so short RPCs avoid a full handshake RTT. Linux exposes it via `net.ipv4.tcp_fastopen` bits: client=1, server=2, both=3. This chapter reads the sysctl from procfs.

## Mental model

```text
  first connection: SYN + cookie request
  later: SYN + data + cookie
```

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| 0 | off |
| 1 | client |
| 2 | server |
| 3 | client+server |

## Worked examples

```
=== /proc/sys net.ipv4.tcp_fastopen ===
1
/proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_fastopen
/proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_fastopen_blackhole_timeout_sec
/proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_fastopen_key
/proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_fastopen=1
/proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_fastopen_blackhole_timeout_sec=0
/proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_fastopen_key=
=== ss ===
State  Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port  Peer Address:Port
LISTEN 0      128        127.0.0.1:8791       0.0.0.0:*   
LISTEN 0      100          0.0.0.0:6080       0.0.0.0:*   
LISTEN 0      100          0.0.0.0:6081       0.0.0.0:*   
LISTEN 0      32         127.0.0.1:5904       0.0.0.0:*   
LISTEN 0      32         127.0.0.1:5900       0.0.0.0:*   
LISTEN 0      32         127.0.0.1:5902       0.0.0.0:*   
LISTEN 0      5            0.0.0.0:2375       0.0.0.0:*   
6.12.94+
```

This guest has **`tcp_fastopen=1`** (client enabled).

## Trap

**Enabling server TFO without measuring.** Some middleboxes blackhole TFO (`tcp_fastopen_blackhole_timeout_sec`).

## Boring rule

Keep client TFO on if the distro default says so. Turn on server TFO only behind metrics and with app support.

## Try this

1. Compare app docs for `TCP_FASTOPEN`.
2. Watch TCPFastOpen counters under load.
3. Read RFC 7413.
